description: The Public Service Commission of the District of Columbia, in Formal Case No. EA2022-04, by Order No. 23134, dated July 29, 2026, granted the request of The Eric Ryan Corporation (“Applicant”) to surrender its electricity supplier license. Cancellation of the Applicant’s electricity supplier license is effective upon the issuance of this Order.

FORMAL CASE NO. EA2022-04, IN THE MATTER OF THE APPLICATION OF THE 
ERIC RYAN CORPORATION TO SURRENDER ITS ELECTRICITY SUPPLIER 
LICENSE IN THE DISTRICT OF COLUMBIA, Order No. 23134 

I. 
INTRODUCTION 
1. 
By this Order,1 the Public Service Commission of the District of Columbia 
(“Commission”) grants the request of The Eric Ryan Corporation (“TERC” or “Applicant”) to 
surrender its electricity supplier license. Cancellation of the Applicant’s electricity supplier license 
is effective upon the issuance of this Order. 

II. 
BACKGROUND 
2. 
On October 25, 2022, the Commission granted TERC a license to operate as an 
electricity supplier in the District of Columbia (“District”) in Order No. 21547.2 On May 18, 2026, 
TERC filed an Application with the Commission to surrender its electricity supplier license.3 
TERC was approved to operate as a broker of electricity services, but it conducts no business as 
TERC and has no customers in the District.4 Consequently, TERC requests to surrender its 
electricity supplier license.5 

1

III. 
DISCUSSION 

3. 
According to 15 DCMR § 4602.10 (a)(1), a licensed electricity supplier wishing to 
cease providing services in the District is required to provide written notice to the Commission of 
the licensee’s intention to cease providing electricity service to its customers and inform its 
customers of the choice to revert to the default service provider or another electricity supplier. 
Section 4602.10 (a)(2) also requires that the surrendering licensee provide to the Commission an 
example or copy of the notice it provided to its customers and, upon the Commission’s receipt of 
such notice, may order the licensee to provide such further notice to its customers or the public as 
the Commission deems necessary, and/or take such other action that the Commission considers 
appropriate.6 

4. 
In the instant case, TERC’s Application provides the required notice to the 
Commission of its intention to surrender its electricity supplier license.7 TERC also states that it 
provided notice to customers, and has attached a sample customer notice, that it no longer conducts 
business as The Eric Ryan Corporation and has transferred its obligations to Renodis ER, LLC.8 
Accordingly, TERC’s Application satisfies the notice requirement with regard to the cessation of 
service. 

5. 
In all other respects, TERC’s Application conforms with Commission 
requirements for a surrendering licensee. Commission records confirm the Applicant’s submission 
of the case number, order number, and date the Applicant’s license was granted.9 TERC avers, 
and Commission records confirm that the Applicant’s most recent survey response indicates no 
jurisdictional revenue and that it owes no outstanding debt or fees.10 In addition, the Applicant 
states that it has no outstanding consumer complaints.11 Lastly, the signed Application from an 
officer of TERC attests to the truth and accuracy of the information submitted.12 

6. 
Based upon the preceding information, the Commission grants TERC’s request to 
surrender its electricity supplier license granted by Order No. 21547. Cancellation of TERC’s 
electricity supplier license shall become effective upon the issuance of this Order. Should TERC 
seek to re-enter the District’s electricity market in the future, it shall have to reapply for an 
electricity supplier license pursuant to Chapter 46 of the Commission’s rules.
